sentences.text: Shri Rajesh Kumr Sen - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri K.S. Patel - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State
Shri Shiv Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the respondent No.2.

Heard on I.A. No.26315/2025 which is first application under Section 430 (1) of BNSS, 2023/389(1)
of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 20.09.2022 passed by the learned Third Additional Sessions Judge, Nainpur, District Mandla (M.P.) in SC No.42/2018, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 366/34, 368/34 and 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.1000/-; R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.1000/-; and R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulation.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the present appellant has been implicated falsely in this case.

entities.text: Third Additional Sessions Judge, Nainpur, District Mandla (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: No DNA report is on record.
As far as FSL report is concerned, it is on record but not supportive because DNA report is not there.

It is also submitted that the prosecutrix herself has admitted in her cross-examination that she is 21 years of age and her statement has been taken after a year, therefore on the date of commission of offence she was major.
It is also submitted that the learned Trial Court has erroneously come to the conclusion that the prosecutrix was 2 CRA-9633-2022 less than 18 years of age.
It is also submitted that no offence as alleged has been committed by the present appellant.
It is a case of consensual relationship and at the time of commission of offence, the prosecutrix was above 18 years of age.
As per the statement of concerned doctor, there was no external injury on the person of the prosecutrix.
The appellant is in custody since 20.09.2022 i.e. from the date of judgment.
It has been admitted by the father of the prosecutrix in para 34 of his cross-examination that there was previous rivalry.
It is further submitted that one another case is pending against the appellant but he has been falsely implicated in that case.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.

It is also submitted that the present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal and, looking to the period of custody, benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted and the appellant may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel appearing for the victim have opposed the prayer made by the appellant on the ground that the present appellant has been convicted for sentence of 10 years RI and fine under Section 376 of IPC.
He has also been convicted under Section 5 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
The minimum sentence is 10 years provided in the aforesaid penal sections.

It is also submitted that the Trial Court after perusing the record has rightly held that the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age at the time of incident and, therefore, has rightly convicted the present appellant under Section 5 & 6 of the POCSO Act, therefore, the contention that it is a consensual relationship between the prosecutrix and 3 CRA-9633-2022 appellant is not tenable.
It is also submitted that ample evidence is on record.
There is no ground to suspend the jail sentence and release the present appellant on bail.
The prosecutrix and other witnesses who are family members of the prosecutrix remained intact in their cross-examination.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the rival contentions of the parties, evidence available on record and having regard to the attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that this is not a fit case for suspension of sentence at this stage.
Accordingly, I.A. No.26315/2025 is dismissed.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE DV Umesh Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154953271/
